So I would -- I ask the interpreters to stick to the written translation because I don't think it's wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says: "Armed forces of the Serbian people west of the Drina and Danube rivers, preserve territorial integrity of the RS and RSK" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could know where Mr. Lukic is right now at least in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Plan of operations and objectives of manoeuvres."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, exactly, it's heading 2 or paragraph 2. [In English] "Plan of operations and objectives ..." [Interpretation] And if you could turn the page, I don't want to read out the entire document, so the next page of the English version. And in the Serbian version we can read combat-readiness of the Army of Yugoslavia repel a potential aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the notion of combat-readiness of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now you must tell us where you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you must go back to the previous page in the English because it starts on the previous page. I wanted to avoid it, but this has already taken more time than it would have if I had read it out all. Perhaps ... [In English] By combat-readiness of the Yugoslav Army of prevent potential aggressors from endangering territorial --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, we're with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I'm actually only interested in the notion of combat-readiness of the VJ. What does it include, and what actions of the VJ are meant by that? What is its task?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In simple terms, the VJ in certain areas must have part of its forces in full combat-readiness, and combat-readiness can be either peacetime readiness, heightened combat-readiness, or full combat-readiness. Full combat-readiness means that the units are ready to start carrying out a combat assignment when ordered to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what follows now are -- what is envisaged in case of Croatian aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we now please see page 8 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you now please tell us what the FRY does in that case or is supposed to do. And I'm going to read it out. In your version it's on page 7, sir. Now I'm reading the following: "In the FRY using stand-by forces, close off axes leading from the neighbouring state deep into the territory, vigorously strike at the root potential armed rebellion in crisis areas in the shortest possible time, conduct mobilisation and strategic development, while part of the forces in co-ordinated action with the SVK is to crush the attack of the aggressor in Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem, and the VRS in the Drina Valley and in Eastern Herzegovina." I'll ask a question about what I have just read out. When Operation Flash happened in May 1995, did the VJ act in accordance with this document? Did it act in co-ordination with the forces of the SVK?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you -- this may be clear, but let me ask you nonetheless. What does acting and co-ordination mean in military terminology?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In military terminology that means that two neighbouring units, in this case two neighbouring armies, should jointly act in performing a mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are they on equal footing there, or is one subordinated to the other?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case they are on equal footing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you will bear with me for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the break I will be able to tell whether I have a correction to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let us look at page 10 of the B/C/S and page 10 of the English. We are now dealing with the tasks of the armed forces --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just interrupt a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you leave this topic. Are you able to tell us, Mr. Simic, why the VJ did not act according to this direction during Operation Flash?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it didn't because this document is not the genuine plan of use of the VJ. It is -- it belongs to the realm of strategic masking and camouflage, which I spoke about. We looked at the Neva missile system, and this is exactly what we wanted to achieve with this directive as regards the adversary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You wanted to achieve -- what was achieved by Operation Flash, that Western Srem and Eastern Slavonia be attacked and you don't come to the rescue, or am I misunderstanding you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to be clearer. This plan was made with the attention to deceive. We wanted to have the adversary think that Yugoslavia would enter the war if the Croatian army attacks the Republic of Serbian Krajina, which means that this -- the character of this plan is a deterrent, just like that model deterred play -- airplanes. In the same fashion we wanted to threaten the adversary that we would enter the war if they commit an act of aggression against the Republic of Serbia and Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see. So you let this document slip into the hands of the enemy so that he can -- the enemy can see what the camouflage says?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, he didn't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: General, you have just said that the two armies participated on equal footing. Could you elaborate on this. Is equal footing in practice or in theory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're speaking about three equal armies. I'm now speaking about the Republic of Serbian Krajina because there is this link with Flash in Western Slavonia. They are two equal and separate armies, and co-ordination is achieved between two neighbours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: In your experience, in the various meetings of the three armies, could you testify that both of -- the three of them acted on equal footing, that no one of them had more power than the other two? Or could you identify the one who really carries the power to decide at the end of the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In practice every army made decisions for itself. The General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia for the Army of Yugoslavia, the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska for its own army, and the Main Staff of the Serb Army of Krajina for its own army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: I again repeat the question. If there were no unanimity in the decision to be taken, who was the ruling vote, the deciding hand, if any?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do beg your pardon. I did not understand your question. Does it pertain to this specific directive or to general practice?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: General, you have before said that you had participated in various concerted meetings at various points, you know, or carrying out tasks in relation to these meetings. My question is: In cases of discrepancies in formulating plans of actions, directives, and so on, when there was discrepancy how these discrepancies were solved? Was there one predominant voice to decide the issue or not? Or the three parties were always on equal footing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge David, these armies were always separate and equal. One was not superior or subordinate to another. In your question you mentioned co-ordination. Let us please bear in mind the following: Co-ordination is resolved in terms of a specific moment in life, whereas this is a document that is done at a very high level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think you will have to keep your question until after the break, Mr. Lukic, if you don't mind. And for the sake of the need to do transcript corrections, we'll come back at ten past -- I beg your pardon, at five to 6.00 instead of quarter to. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have on our screens -- or rather, I saw a problem in the transcript. It's nothing drastic so I'm not going to raise the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 17 in B/C/S and page 17 in English, General, in your copy it's page 16.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what was the page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says 16 in your document, the last page of the directive. Let's just wait for the English version to appear on our screens. The document was signed by the president of the Supreme Defence Council, Mr. Zoran Lilic. That's right, isn't it? And it has the seal of -- well, I can't see exactly what seal it is, but there is a stamp, a seal, at any rate, right next to the signature?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the English version the signature is on the next page if you want to have a look at it, but I think that what I discussed just now can be seen in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move into closed session for a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session -- closed session, not private.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Closed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that one plan of use has three elements; namely, a directive, a map decision, and an action plan. Did I remember that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, these are three basic parts from which the operationalisation of all other attachments is derived. This is just one that we've read out, but at any rate it is the most important part of the directive. I stand corrected, the main part of the plan of use.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we are going to look at Prosecution Exhibit P1563. Could we please have page 10 on our screens. The witness is going to tell us what this is, and then I'm going to tell you, Your Honours, what my intention was, how I'm going to do this with the witness. I hope that the Trial Chamber will find this to be of benefit. Would you just tell us, General, what this is. We are going to zoom in a bit.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is from the directive, and it is entitled - you can read it up here - "Expected Model Of Attack." This is related to the air force.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there is an English translation of the text on the map, but I'm afraid that you will not be able to follow this. I would suggest that we read what these parts of the map say and it's going to be easier for you to follow in this way what it is that I want to put to the witness. Can we have a look at page 9 of this document. On the other pages we actually see parts of the map. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, General, you see this down here, what does it say? Who is the signatory, and has this document been signed at all?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was written up by an air-force man, commander of the RV and the PVO of the air force, Major-General Milivoj Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just take it easy. Did he sign this part here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could we have page 6 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was supposed to approve this document? I'm going to read this out -- or rather, you read out what is written in the upper left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I hereby approve, Chief of Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, Lieutenant-General Momcilo Perisic."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he sign this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More specifically, whether he approved it; no, he did not approve this document because he did not sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have page 19 of this exhibit, could we have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out what is written there or perhaps if it's easier for you I can read it out.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decision for the joint use of armed forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this document signed anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go back to page 18 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see anything here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I assume and know that it was not approved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 24, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Judge Moloto.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. You can't assume and know, you either assume or you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume from the point of view that I did not see it on the screen, and I know that the -- that it was not approved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I still say you can't do both. You either know or you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is entitled "Plan of use of forces of the air force and air support against 'D.'"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 20 of this document where a certain part is enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the left-hand corner it says: "I hereby approve, Chief of General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, Lieutenant-General Momcilo Perisic." Is his signature there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, in order for this directive to be carried out in practice, what else had to be done after this directive had been written up so that the plan of use could function?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order for the plan of use to be valid and for it to be able to take effect if necessary, as I've already said, this textual part has to be materialised through the decision and the action plan. Through the other attachments it should be operationalised in greater detail, or rather, the set tasks should be operationalised. We can see here that the participants in the elaboration of this document signed this document, but it was not approved by the Chief of General Staff. When I spoke about plans of use, I said that a decision has to be approved by the president and the plan has to be signed by the assistant Chief of General Staff and approved by the Chief of General Staff. In this specific case the directive was signed by the president of the Supreme Defence Council, but all other necessary documents, I mean for the plan to -- or rather, in order to make it possible for those who are supposed to carry out -- to carry it out in that way, it was simply not elaborated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry, can we see where the participants in the elaboration of this document signed, please. If you can scroll, let's see where the signatures are on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we go back to page 24, I believe that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Lukic. The witness is talking about this page, and he's saying that the participants in the elaboration signed this page, and I want to see the signature of this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I wanted. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You say we must go to another page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's because the image that we saw earlier is just one enlarged portion of this, which is the whole document. This is the whole map and what we saw earlier was only part of it. I believe that the witness will be able to provide an answer and now that he can see the entire map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Who are the signatories, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is the plan of use for the forces of the anti-aircraft defence, and it was signed by the commander of the air force and anti-aircraft defence, Major-General Milivoj Pavlovic, commander of the air force and anti-aircraft defence as I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the break you were explaining to Judge Moloto, following up on my question about Operation Flash why no action was taken, and you answered that question. While you were working on this document, did you believe that you were working on a genuine plan of use.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the very beginning of my work on this plan, I fostered some doubts as to the seriousness of these documents because the methodology of working out a war plan or plan of use was not adhered to. When I spoke generally about a plan of use, I said that there must be an organisational order which regulates what is to be done, by who, where, how, et cetera. And that all participants were required to sign special declarations about keeping state secrets, just as I made a solemn declaration here. But that wasn't respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. I have a follow-up question. Does that mean that you, participants who were working on this document, did not sign such solemn declarations as are usually signed before starting work on a plan of use?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and once we had elaborated the directive and these few attachments, subsequent work was interrupted suddenly. I knew that something was wrong, and I asked my superior officer, the late General Kovacevic, I asked him jokingly, "Blagoje, what is this about?" And he replied to me calmly, "Simke you know the same that I know, and don't ask questions, do what you're told to do." And then I understood that something was wrong with regard to the completeness and the seriousness of the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did any part of the Drina plan ever become effective in the VJ from 1993 on?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this plan, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you replied to Judge Moloto about strategic camouflage, did anybody tell you that the idea behind this plan was strategic camouflage, or was something else the matter?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is camouflage at the highest strategic level so that only the Supreme Defence Council and possibly the Chief of General Staff were the only ones that were privy to the real intentions behind this plan. Nobody else was allowed to know what objective -- what the objective of this plan was. If it hadn't been that way, the goal of deception couldn't have been achieved.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) And finally, none of those who should have been tasked with implementing the plan was ever sent an extract to enable them to elaborate their own plans. While I was working on this, I did not know that the real intention was deception, but later on Flash, Storm, and what is written there clearly indicated to me that the high state authorities wanted to deter Croatia from attacking the RSK in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would request a correction on page 61 of the transcript from lines 12 till line 16. Only that should be redacted. We can leave the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You want a redaction of lines 12 to 16 on page 61? Can we do that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up to line 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, Mr. Simic, if I understand how your testimony thus far, you can't say while I was working on this, I did not know that the real intention was deception. You must have known right from the beginning, and I'll tell you why, which is one of the reasons you've given us why you say this was deception, because you didn't make a declaration before you did this job, number one. At the end, the chief of the General Staff didn't sign this plan. So in addition to the couple of reasons that you have given us is that two other reasons, one of which you were aware of before you started the job, so you knew at the beginning that this was camouflage because you did not make a declaration before you started the job. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, not fully. When I with my colleagues started elaborating this plan, nobody told me explicitly, "You are working on a plan of deception," because if that had been communicated to a group of people, the purpose of the plan couldn't have been achieved. The intelligence services would have come by the information that this is a plan for deception purposes, but even then I had my doubts, or rather, I had some knowledge about that being the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand all that, Mr. Simic. All I'm saying is that from the position you held and from your general knowledge of the procedures for a genuine plan you knew that for a genuine plan before the participants can participate they make a solemn declaration to keep state secrets. You were not made to make such a declaration when you started this job. So from your general knowledge you could assess, even as you asked your superior, Kovacevic, "What is this for," I'm sure it was a rhetorical question. You knew that this was not genuine based on your own evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, Your Honour, that I knew it at the time. But nobody had told me so explicitly from above, no one -- none of my superiors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I suspect that, because as you rightly say if anybody told you then it defeats the whole purpose of the plan. So you've got to read in between the lines, and as a senior officer, I'm sure it was virtually on the lines for you, not in between.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have finished with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, have you heard of the Gvozd plan?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except during the proofing with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before I showed you the document we're about to discuss, you had never heard about it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see document P494 on the screen. I again have a hard copy for General Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's wait for it to appear on the screen. General, as compared to the document that we saw earlier, the Drina directive, please look at page 1 here and tell us whether you see any differences between this document and that one when it comes to the format of the first page.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 1 is exactly the same as that of any directive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this directive have a registry stamp?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can be on the cover page, but it can also be inside the directive. But there is no stamp showing that it was registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the Drina directive we saw the stamp of your first administration, but we cannot see one here. Please turn to page 18 of the B/C/S version. I believe that I got the page right this time. It's the last-but-one page. It's page 19 in the B/C/S. In the English we'll find it, it's the last-but-one page. Yes. We have seen on the Drina directive a signature and a round stamp. Does this document also bear a round stamp?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not only is the round stamp missing, which round stamp means the verification of the validity of the document, but there's also the name of the supreme commander of the SVK missing because his name should have been mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe that a short while ago when you were answering questions about the Drina plan and the rules as governing the number of copies of the plan to be produced, are such rules in force for all plans and directives?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that a directive is made for either the entire war or for a longer period of the war and reflects the positions of the highest authorities of the state with regard to the waging of war. This directive is made operational by orders issued by lower levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it in accordance with this doctrine that copies are produced without an indication which copy it is out of how many. Maybe we can return to the cover page. Wait a minute, please. The Trial Chamber must be able to see. Let us see the cover page in the B/C/S also. With regard to the importance of such a document, can such a document be produced without an indication of which copy it is out of how many?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already mentioned that a directive is made in two copies. And in case of war activities, one copy is kept in the principal command post and another copy in the secondary command post if one of them should be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is the number indicating which copy it is mentioned on each such document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were able to read the document while I was showing it to you. Do you know, General, whether anybody from the General Staff of the VJ from your administration took part in the production of this document -- but no, you said that you knew nothing about the document. Do you know that any of your subordinates went to co-operate with anybody from the SVK in making such a directive?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody from the first administration went to work on such a document, otherwise I would have had to know because an order of mine was required for them to be able to go there and carry out their task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anybody else in the General Staff of the VJ work on such documents without belonging to the first administration?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the main task of the first administration, and no one else can go and work on such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the last page in B/C/S and in English. I haven't got the number, but I hope we'll find our way. I think it's page 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, in this document, General, certain units are mentioned. You see here in line 2 -- well, actually why don't you read these numbers slowly because there are a lot of abbreviations here, and please tell us whose units they are, the units mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this specific document that I have in my hands it is stated that this is an annex to the plan of use of the Serbian army of Krajina, and in the task for the 11th Corps it says, The 11th Corps with Operations Group 2 (18th and 138th Motorised Brigade, 453rd, and 1st Armoured Brigade, 51st Mechanised Brigade, 16th Motorised Brigade, 12th Mixed Anti-tank Artillery Battalion, 1st Artillery Battalion of the 240th medium self-propelled air defence rocket regiment, and 155th Light Infantry Brigade). Obviously this is some kind of a newly-formed command of a temporary composition, that's why it was called Operations Group 2. These units are units of the Army of Yugoslavia, more specifically of the Novi Sad Corps of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us be specific. This 11th Corps that is mentioned in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 11th Corps is a corps of the Serb army of Krajina. However, according to this annex the commander, or rather, the elaborating party reinforced that corps with an operations group consisting of these units that I mentioned, that I read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know, General, whether any one of the units mentioned here ever received this document or excerpts from this document on the basis of which they would know what their possible task might be?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the methodology of work, this 11th Corps which got this operative group on the basis of this document would have to go to its own plan of use and provide an extract from it to the commander of the operations group so that that commander of the operations group could work out an order for the implementation of this task for each and every one of the units mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I appreciate that you might probably be understanding each other, but, Mr. Simic, can I ask you to please listen very carefully to the questions put to you and answer the question that is put to you. The question put to you is: Did any one of these components of the operation group receive either this document or excerpts from this document so that he or she knows what his task is supposed to be? Now, a direct answer to that question is: Yes, somebody did receive; or no, nobody received it; or I don't know. That long sentence that you gave really -- it skirts around the question, and we never know what the actual answer to the question is. It makes it very difficult at the end of the day to know what you actually intended to say. And we rely on what you are telling us to come to a conclusion at the end of this case. Now, can you answer that question: Did any one of the components of the operational group receive this document or excerpts from this document so that he or she knows what his task is going to be to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there was no command of Operations Group 2, and none of these units received any extracts regarding this task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General Simic, please just give me a yes or a no now in response to my next question. Your operations administration, would it have to have information of this nature if your VJ units were to be attached to someone else? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything else here - I don't want to lead - but is there anything else on this page, in this document, that is contrary to military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the composition of units of this operation group 2 there is a reference to the 16th Motorised Brigade. And towards the bottom the penultimate sentence says, Support AV and PVO and 16th Motorised Brigade. This has to do with support. A motorised brigade cannot provide support if it's a motorised brigade. What he probably meant was the 16th Artillery Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are not going to speculate now. Can one and the same unit be both in an operations group and in the support force?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done in this document. Let us move on. We're going to move on to a completely different subject. General, are you tired? Can we continue working?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not for me to decide about that. It is for the honourable Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you say you are tired, we will take that into account. We have 15 minutes to go before we end the day. Can you carry on for another 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you can, I can too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. General, we have quite a few documents, and I would like to move through them quickly. We are going back to the operations centre to specific information and specific reports. I'm going to show you document -- it's from the Defence 65 ter list 00668D -- actually, since I'm sure that we're going to be dealing with these documents tomorrow as well, but if the Prosecutor agrees, could we have an entire set of documents placed before Mr. Simic because he will have to deal with a series of very short documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It would be helpful if we could see them one at a time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I meant, but I thought that the entire set of documents should be there with Mr. Simic so that we wouldn't have to go all the way through the courtroom rather than giving them to him one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought the OTP could have a look. Yes, that's right, yes, yes. A few today. Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just understand you. You're not suggesting that we give him those documents overnight. You're suggesting that tomorrow you give him a batch of documents which the Prosecution will have seen --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. Yes, tomorrow, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Bear in mind you've got to give them an opportunity to go through those documents first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. [Interpretation] We've already provided them with a list and they are aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, let us look at this document in front of you. What is this? Actually, my first question is: What is this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is information from the intelligence administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Who is it being provided to? You can see it down here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Submitted to the Chief of General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, the operations centre of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, and intelligence organs of the commands of armies and the immediate subordinate units related to the Chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this information one of the sources that later becomes part of what is known as the daily operations report of the operations centre?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The information is dated the 1st of May, 1995. Do you know what it refers to? Just one sentence?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that at that time the aggression against Western Slavonia, the Republic of Serb Krajina took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please receive a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit Number D212.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document I'd like to show to the General is [In English] 65 ter 00669D. [Interpretation] Let us just wait for the document so that the Trial Chamber can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a document similar to the previous one. It also pertains to the same period. Let us just clarify this for the Trial Chamber. Where can we see on this document that your operations centre is a recipient of this document too?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Down here in the lower left-hand corner it says, OC of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please receive a number and then we can move on. We don't need to comment upon it for the time being. I think that this will do for the time being, and then we'll deal with other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is Exhibit Number D213.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is 65 ter number [In English] 00695D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like us to comment upon this document. It says here, Report, and the previous document said, Information. In essence is this something we should pay attention to or not? It's the second administration again, right, the intelligence information that is providing this document, and it was submitted to your centre? It's not that I want to lead but --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where do we see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you scroll down the English version. I don't want to lead. The next page, Your Honour. Do you see the end?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, sorry, we'll have to deal with this document a bit longer. Why is this document called Report and the previous one was called Information? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In essence there is no difference between information and intelligence report. That was information due to the urgency of the problem at hand, and it is sent to the Chief of General Staff. So therefore, it has more specific weight in terms of the security of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Here the processing person thought that that was not the case and he simply sent it to the operations centre and through the daily operations -- through the daily operations report, the Chief of General Staff will be made aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the previous English page back, and I'm going to read one sentence out. The date of this document is the 7th of July, 1995, and we see that there is a reference to the forces of the 1st Corps of the Muslim army, right, and then there is the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th, and 7th Corps of the Muslim army. And now the sentence says -- the sentence I'm interested in is the following one. Your Honours, it's towards the middle of the page. "The Muslim forces in the enclaves of Gorazde, Zepa, and Srebrenica are maintaining a high level of combat-readiness and have intensified reconnaissance, sabotage, and surprise operations against the VRS." That's what is written here. I had to read this so that we don't have to put the document here twice. The information from this document, is it entered into the daily operations report as deemed relevant by the processing party?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to look at the daily operations report of that day, but first could we have an exhibit number for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit Number D214.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this was a document dated the 7th of July, 1995. Now let us look at [In English] 00489D. [Interpretation] It's a document from the 65 ter list of the Defence. I thought this was a document that is directly linked to the previous one, but no, it's another. You are about to receive the next document, sir. Let us now wait for the document to appear to enable the Trial Chamber to look at it. General, this is what we have mentioned several times, both yesterday and today. What kind of document is this, judging by its format, and what does such a document contain?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a daily operations report which is made in the operations centre of the General Staff of the VJ. It contains under 1, the activities of the armed forces of neighbouring countries; under 2, situation along the state border; and then it deals with attempts to cross the border illegally; under 3, we can see the situation, activities, and changes in the units of the VJ. Here in this item the units mentioned are the 1st Army and others. Under 4, we can see extraordinary events, and there was one such event in the 2nd Army. There was an extraordinary event in the General Staff and then there were searches and the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this a format according to which every daily operations report was made?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can we see the time-period covered by the report?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just ask you for a comment about this document. This is dated the 9th of July, 1995, and the activities of the armed forces of neighbouring countries are also mentioned. But what I'm really interested in is the situation on the state border. Under 2 it says: "On the 8th of July the monitoring mission of the UN visited the border post of Zavina of the 16th Battalion from Bajina Basta and they had no remarks or no objections." Where is Bajina Basta, which country does it border on?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The small town of Bajina Basta is in the valley of the Drina River which is western Serbia. It borders on the Republika Srpska. And we received this report from the 1st Army as this border battalion, the 16th, the command of which is in Bajina Basta, sent it to the command of the army, and we extracted it from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The exhibit is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D215.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we break for today, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sure we can, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Simic, I know you know, however, it is my duty to warn you again that you may not talk to anybody while you are in the witness stand about the case, and especially your lawyers. We'll come back in the same court tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of February, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
